summary: Mount Spokane summit tower: a 40-ft DNR live-in tower built 1979, last staffed 1994, scrapped 2001; its cab was set on a new tower on Quartz Mountain in 2004.

facts.design: 40-foot timber DNR live-in tower (1979); firelookout.com ties an L-4 cab to the 1950 45-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: The 1979 summit tower was scrapped in June 2001; its cab was set on a new 10-foot tower on Quartz Mountain in 2004.

staffing.status: Last staffed in 1994; permanently decommissioned that year

facts.agency: Washington Dept. of Natural Resources; Mt. Spokane State Park

access.note: The Quartz Mountain cab is rented through Washington State Parks by reservation, summer only, with a two-night minimum. The summit tower is gone.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in or bike-in only: a 2.7-mile trail from parking at Selkirk Lodge to the Quartz Mountain cab.

events.note: The Forest Service offered a lookout building, on condition that a man be placed in charge during fire season.
Second-floor dormer of the stone Vista House, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, served as the first lookout.
A forest service lookout on the mountain telephoned in the location of four fires during a lightning storm.
An 85-foot wood tower was built and collapsed in its first winter under heavy snow.
A 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab was built.
The 1950 tower was replaced by a 40-foot timber DNR live-in tower.
The Washington DNR built a 40-foot timber live-in tower on the summit of Mount Spokane.
The 1979 tower was last staffed and was permanently decommissioned.
In June 2001 crews scrapped the tower; the 9,000-pound cab was lifted by crane and moved by truck to a ranger's residence.
In late August 2004 the cab was set atop a new 10-foot tower on Quartz Mountain.
The Quartz Mountain lookout joined a rental program.
The Quartz Mountain lookout was registered April 13, 2022, as US 1558, WA 85.

corrections.why: Both sources give 40 feet for the 1979 summit tower. 13.7 m is about 45 feet, which is the height of the 1950 pole tower.
Firelookout.com ties the L-4 cab to the 1950 45-foot pole tower and describes the 1979 tower as a 40-foot timber DNR live-in tower. No source read calls the 1979 tower an L-4.

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to Quartz Mountain.)
corrections.proposed: Tower scrapped June 2001; cab set on a new 10-foot tower on Quartz Mountain in 2004
corrections.why: The record holds a placeholder string rather than dated events.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief notes firelookout.com says standing. The firelookout.com page for this site says the 1979 tower was dismantled in 2001, and firelookout.org lists the summit tower as gone. The story treats the summit tower as gone and the cab as standing on Quartz Mountain.

Firelookout.com says the cab and part of the tower were rebuilt on Quartz Mountain in 2004. The NHLR and TrailChick say the cab alone was set on a new 10-foot tower. The story follows the NHLR and notes the difference.

sources.title: Mount Spokane Quartz Mountain Fire Lookout

notes_for_editor: The core dates (1979 build, 1994 last staffing, 2001 scrapping, 2004 move) agree across firelookout.com, the NHLR and TrailChick. The 2004 rebuild detail and the 40-versus-45-foot height are the points to check. Named lookouts (Adelia Blake, 1945 to 1955) come from firelookout.com's personnel list; the story names only one. The 1937 fire report is from a newspaper transcription on washingtonlookouts.weebly.com, not from the original paper. The parks page gives no price and points to a separate fee page, which was not read, so the $100 figure is the NHLR's. Related records us-wa-mount-spokane-at-quartz-mountain (existing story) and us-wa-mount-spokane-vista-house cover the same tower and the Vista House; cross-link when published.
